## Detailed comparisons

- [Rupok vs Note3](https://rupok.app/compare/note3/): A free alternative to Prestigio’s Windows-only EasiNote successor.
- [Rupok vs SMART Notebook](https://rupok.app/compare/smart-notebook/): Every feature free, on any brand of board.
- [Rupok vs OpenBoard](https://rupok.app/compare/openboard/): Two free, open-source whiteboards, side by side.
- [Jamboard alternative](https://rupok.app/compare/jamboard/): Jamboard shut down in 2024. Bring your Jams back as PDFs.
- [Rupok vs Microsoft Whiteboard](https://rupok.app/compare/microsoft-whiteboard/): No account needed, after the 2026 app retirement.
- [Rupok vs ActivInspire](https://rupok.app/compare/activinspire/): Free with every feature, in the browser or on the desktop.
- [Rupok vs Explain Everything](https://rupok.app/compare/explain-everything/): Unlimited stroke replay instead of short videos.
- [Rupok vs OneNote](https://rupok.app/compare/onenote/): A notebook vs a tool for presenting at the board.

## How we compare

- We only use the other product’s own pages (pricing, release notes, help centre, app store listing), and say when a source is a mirror or a reseller copy.
- Every claim has a date. Software changes; if we’re out of date, [tell us on GitHub](https://github.com/Shaitrish/rupok/issues) and we’ll fix it.
- We say where the other product is stronger. Rupok is young: some features (live class, Rupok Cloud, Bangla interface) are still coming, and we label them that way.
- No logos, no made-up numbers.

## Questions people ask

### What is the best smartboard software?

It depends on your boards and what you teach. SMART Notebook and ActivInspire suit schools invested in SMART or Promethean hardware. OpenBoard is a solid free desktop app. Rupok is free, open source and works on any board, with AI-made interactive lessons and class replay.

### What is the best free smartboard software?

The free options are Rupok and OpenBoard (both open source), plus the free basic editions of SMART Notebook and ActivInspire. Only Rupok and OpenBoard are free with every feature on any brand of board.

### Is there open-source smartboard software?

Yes: Rupok (AGPL-3.0, runs in the browser and as a desktop app) and OpenBoard (GPL-3.0, desktop app).

### Which whiteboard software supports Bangla?

Rupok supports Bangla text and fonts in lessons today, and its Bangla interface is coming. Note3, SMART Notebook, OpenBoard, ActivInspire and Explain Everything don’t list Bangla among their interface languages. Microsoft 365 apps such as OneNote offer Bangla proofing tools and partial Bangla (India) localization.

---

# A free Note3 alternative: Rupok vs Note3

> Looking for a free alternative to Prestigio Note3 (EasiNote) whiteboard software? Compare price, platforms, AI, replay and Bangla support. Facts checked November 2026.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/note3/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

Note3 is Prestigio’s paid, Windows-only whiteboard software, the updated EasiNote. Rupok is free and open source, runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on any computer or as a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux, and adds AI-made lessons and class replay. Here’s an honest comparison.

## Rupok vs Note3 at a glance

*Rupok and Note3 compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | Note3 |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ✗ Paid, one-time licence per device: €29 on Prestigio’s store (Nov 2026), after a 15-day trial[^1][^3] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✗ No |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | Windows only. Prestigio’s Android panels need a connected Windows PC[^1][^2] |
| Account | ✓ None, for teachers or students | Online activation with a serial number[^4] |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ✗ None documented[^2][^4] |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ✗ No stroke replay documented[^4] |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | ✓ Subject tools for maths, physics and chemistry (geometry, circuits, lab apparatus)[^2][^4] |
| Handwriting and shapes | ✓ Smart shapes, offline: hand-drawn shapes, graphs, flowcharts, logic gates, tables and Venn diagrams snap clean. Handwritten maths to LaTeX, offline. Other handwriting to text with your own Claude API key. Bangla handwriting: coming soon | ✓ Handwriting and formula recognition[^4] |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ✓ Imports PDF and PowerPoint; exports PDF, PPTX, DOCX and JPG[^4] |
| Bangla | ◐ Bangla text and fonts in lessons; Bangla voice typing and settings search. Bangla interface: coming soon | ✗ About 29 interface languages in the installer, no Bangla[^4] |
| Offline | ✓ The desktop app works without internet, including maths recognition (AI features need internet). In the browser, the board runs on your device once it is open | ✓ Installed Windows app (activation needs internet)[^4] |
| Smartboards and panels | ✓ Any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari | ✓ Panels, PCs, laptops and projectors running Windows[^2] |
| File format | Open `.rpk` (a ZIP package with a published spec) | `.enb` (the EasiNote format)[^4] |

## Where Note3 is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **Ready-made STEM tools.** Geometry and 3D shapes, electric circuits, chemistry apparatus and the periodic table are built in[^2][^4]. Rupok’s Smart Ink draws clean graphs and logic gates (and, once switched on in Settings, circuit symbols and benzene rings), and its presets gallery has ready-made physics and chemistry objects, but it has no ruler, protractor, compass, lab apparatus or periodic table yet. For those you ask your AI for a Smart Object.
- **Handwriting recognition without an AI account**[^4]. Rupok reads handwritten maths offline, but turning other handwriting into text needs your own Claude API key, and it can’t read Bangla handwriting yet.
- **Opens PowerPoint files directly** and lets you annotate them[^4]. In Rupok you save slides as PDF first.
- **More export formats:** PPTX, DOCX and JPG as well as PDF[^4]. Rupok exports PDF (slides or handouts).
- **Document-camera support**[^4].

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **Free on every device.** No licence keys and no activation, so you can put it on every panel and laptop in your school.
- **Not just Windows.** It runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS, and as a free desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.
- **AI Smart Objects.** Ask Claude or ChatGPT for a simulation or a quiz and it lands on your slide, live, ready to write on.
- **AI help on the board.** Chat with your own Claude, Codex or OpenCode inside Rupok, or select a problem and tap Solve this: the AI writes a step-by-step solution in handwriting, and you check it before the class sees it.
- **Class replay.** Every stroke is saved with its timing. Send the `.rpk` file to the class WhatsApp group; students replay it in their browser.
- **Bangla.** Bangla text and fonts work in lessons, voice typing works in Bangla, and a Bangla interface is coming. Rupok is made in Bangladesh.
- **Open source, open format.** Your lessons are never locked in.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick Note3** if you teach on Windows, rely on its built-in geometry, physics and chemistry tools or on opening PowerPoint files directly, and are happy to buy a licence for each device.

**Pick Rupok** if you want one free tool on every board and laptop, interactive lessons made by AI, and replays your students can open on their phones.

You can also use both: export a Note3 lesson to PDF and teach it in Rupok.

## Switching from Note3

1. **Export from Note3.** Note3 exports lessons as PDF[^4].
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and Note3: questions

### Is there a free alternative to Note3?

Yes. Rupok is free and open source. It runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on any computer connected to your smartboard or panel, with no licence key, activation or account.

### Is Note3 the same as EasiNote?

Prestigio describes Note3 as the updated version of EasiNote, launched in July 2024[^1]. Its files use EasiNote’s `.enb` format[^4].

### Can Rupok open Note3 (.enb) files?

No. Export the lesson from Note3 as a PDF and drop the PDF into Rupok; every page becomes a slide you can write on.

### Does Rupok work on a Prestigio MultiBoard?

Rupok needs Chrome, Edge or Safari with WebGPU or WebGL2. On a panel with a Windows PC module or a connected computer, open rupok.app/board there, or install the Rupok desktop app (Windows, Mac or Linux). Whether a panel’s built-in Android browser is fast enough varies by model, so a PC is the safe choice.

### Is Rupok legal to use for free in schools?

Yes. Rupok is open-source software under the AGPL-3.0. Any school can use it on any number of devices at no cost.

## Sources

Facts about other products were checked on 23 November 2026. Prices and features change; if you spot something out of date, please [open an issue](https://github.com/Shaitrish/rupok/issues).

[^2]: [Note3 interactive whiteboard software](https://prestigio-solutions.com/product/note3-interactive-whiteboard-software), Prestigio Solutions product page (checked 23 Nov 2026).

# A free SMART Notebook alternative for any board

> A free, open-source alternative to SMART Notebook that works on any brand of smartboard. Compare price, platforms, AI, replay and languages, with sources. Checked November 2026.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/smart-notebook/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

SMART Notebook is the most established smartboard software, with a free basic version and paid Plus features. Rupok is free with every feature, open source, and works the same on any brand of panel. Here’s where each one wins.

## Rupok vs SMART Notebook at a glance

*Rupok and SMART Notebook compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | SMART Notebook |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ◐ Basic Notebook is free; Notebook Plus with Lumio Standard is US$59/year[^1]. New installs get a 180-day Plus trial[^4] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✗ No |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | Windows 10/11 and macOS[^3]. No Linux, iPad or Android app (the iPad app ended in 2020)[^5]. Lumio runs in a browser[^6] |
| Account | ✓ None, for teachers or students | Online activation for the desktop app[^3] |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ◐ Lumio AI Assist generates lessons, quizzes and activities, limited on the free plan[^6][^7]. No AI in desktop Notebook release notes through August 2026[^4] |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ◐ Lesson Recorder (Plus) records on-page actions, without sound[^8] |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | ✓ Game templates, assessments and SMART Blocks in Plus[^2]; Lumio games and widgets[^6] |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ✓ Imports PDF, and PowerPoint on Windows[^4] |
| Bangla | ◐ Bangla text and fonts in lessons; Bangla voice typing and settings search. Bangla interface: coming soon | ✗ 38 interface languages on Windows, no Bangla[^3] |
| Offline | ✓ The desktop app works without internet, including maths recognition (AI features need internet). In the browser, the board runs on your device once it is open | ✓ Installed desktop app; some features need internet[^3] |
| Smartboards and panels | ✓ Any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari | ◐ Without Plus, touch on non-SMART displays is limited; Plus works with any brand[^2] |
| Real-time collaboration | ◷ Live class and share links: coming soon with Rupok Cloud | ◐ Student-device activities through Lumio[^6] |
| File format | Open `.rpk` (a ZIP package with a published spec) | `.notebook`; imports ActivInspire `.flipchart` files[^4] |
| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Actively developed: Notebook 26 released May 2026[^4] |

## Where SMART Notebook is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **Decades of classroom use**, and a huge base of `.notebook` lessons shared between teachers.
- **Game-based activities and assessments on student devices** through Lumio, with LMS integrations (Canvas, Schoology, D2L) on the Spark plan[^6].
- **AI lesson and quiz generation is shipping** in Lumio[^7].
- **Deep SMART hardware support:** pens, ink and touch tuned for SMART Boards.
- **Imports ActivInspire flipcharts**, with bulk conversion[^4].

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **Every feature is free, on any brand.** SMART’s free version limits touch on non-SMART displays[^2]; Rupok works the same on a SMART, Promethean, BenQ, ViewSonic or Prestigio panel.
- **Runs on Linux and ChromeOS too**, in Chrome, Edge or Safari with nothing to install, or as a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.
- **AI that builds real simulations,** not only quizzes: projectile motion, 3D molecules, circuits. It works with the AI you already use: chat with Claude, Codex or OpenCode inside Rupok, or connect them through MCP.
- **Class replay students can open.** They replay every stroke from a small `.rpk` file, in the browser, with no account.
- **Bangla text in lessons**, and an open-source codebase and file format.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick SMART Notebook** if your school runs SMART Boards, uses Lumio’s student-device games or LMS integrations, or has years of `.notebook` lessons.

**Pick Rupok** if your boards are mixed brands, you want every feature free, or you want AI-made simulations and class replays.

## Switching from SMART Notebook

1. **Save your Notebook lesson as a PDF.** Export or print it to PDF from SMART Notebook.
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and SMART Notebook: questions

### Is SMART Notebook free?

The basic desktop version is free. Notebook Plus with Lumio Standard costs US$59 a year[^1], and full touch on non-SMART displays needs Plus[^2]. Rupok is free with every feature.

### What is the best free alternative to SMART Notebook?

For a free desktop app with a long history, OpenBoard. For a free app that runs in the browser or on the desktop, with AI-made interactive lessons and class replay, Rupok. Both are open source.

### Can Rupok open .notebook files?

No. Save the lesson as a PDF from SMART Notebook and drop it into Rupok to write on every page.

### Does Rupok work on a SMART Board?

Yes. Rupok runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari on the computer connected to the board, and works with the board’s touch and pen like any browser app.

# Rupok vs OpenBoard: two free, open-source whiteboards

> Rupok and OpenBoard are both free, open-source whiteboard software for teachers. Compare platforms, AI, replay, recording and languages. Facts checked November 2026.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/openboard/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

OpenBoard is a mature, free desktop whiteboard maintained in Geneva. Rupok is a newer free whiteboard that runs in the browser or as a desktop app, with AI-made lessons and stroke-by-stroke replay. Both are open source, so this is about fit, not price.

## Rupok vs OpenBoard at a glance

*Rupok and OpenBoard compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | OpenBoard |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ✓ Free, no registration[^1] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✓ Yes: GPL-3.0[^3] |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | Windows 10+, macOS 12+ and Debian, plus community Linux packages[^3][^4]. No web, ChromeOS or mobile app |
| Account | ✓ None, for teachers or students | ✓ None[^1] |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ✗ None |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ◐ Podcast mode records the board and your voice as a video[^5] |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | ✓ Web widgets and about 25 built-in activities (memory, word games)[^6] |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ✓ Imports and exports PDF[^5]; IWB (Common File Format) import and export[^3] |
| Bangla | ◐ Bangla text and fonts in lessons; Bangla voice typing and settings search. Bangla interface: coming soon | ✗ 35 interface languages, no Bangla translation[^3] |
| Offline | ✓ The desktop app works without internet, including maths recognition (AI features need internet). In the browser, the board runs on your device once it is open | ✓ Installed desktop app[^1] |
| Smartboards and panels | ✓ Any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari | ✓ Any interactive whiteboard, graphics tablet or mouse[^1] |
| File format | Open `.rpk` (a ZIP package with a published spec) | `.ubz`[^5] |
| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Actively maintained: version 1.7.7 released 30 March 2026; 1.8 in development[^2] |

## Where OpenBoard is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **A mature desktop app** for Windows, macOS and Linux, with roots going back to 2003 (Uniboard, then Open-Sankoré)[^1]. Rupok’s desktop app is new: its installers aren’t code-signed yet and the Mac app is in beta.
- **Video recording with sound** (Podcast mode)[^5]. Rupok replays strokes; audio is coming.
- **IWB / Common File Format** import and export, for swapping lessons with other whiteboard software[^3].
- **A library of widgets and activities**, and a widget API[^6].
- **Institutional backing:** maintained with the Canton of Geneva’s public education department[^1].

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **Nothing to install.** It runs in Chrome, Edge or Safari, so it also works on Chromebooks, Macs and locked-down school PCs. Prefer an app? The free desktop app runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.
- **AI Smart Objects.** Live simulations, 3D models and quizzes made by Claude, ChatGPT, Codex or OpenCode, with an MCP server for agents.
- **Stroke-by-stroke replay** in a small lesson file, instead of a large video. Students pause, zoom and still use the live objects.
- **Smart shapes and maths, offline:** hand-drawn shapes, graphs, flowcharts and logic gates snap clean, and handwritten maths becomes typeset LaTeX.
- **GPU ink** that stays smooth with 100,000 strokes.
- **A student viewer** at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/): no account, nothing uploaded.
- **Bangla text and fonts** in lessons.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick OpenBoard** if you want a long-proven desktop app, video recording with sound, or IWB file exchange.

**Pick Rupok** if you want to teach from any browser or the desktop app, add AI-made interactive lessons, or send students replayable classes.

Both are free, so try both on your board for a week.

## Switching from OpenBoard

1. **Export from OpenBoard.** OpenBoard exports documents as PDF[^5].
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and OpenBoard: questions

### What is a good OpenBoard alternative?

If you want to stay free and open source, Rupok is the closest: same price (free), plus AI Smart Objects and stroke replay, running in the browser or as a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.

### Is OpenBoard still maintained?

Yes. Version 1.7.7 came out on 30 March 2026, and 1.8 is in development[^2].

### Can Rupok open .ubz files?

No. Export the document from OpenBoard as a PDF and drop it into Rupok.

### Which licence do they use?

OpenBoard is GPL-3.0[^3]. Rupok is AGPL-3.0, and its `.rpk` file format spec is Apache-2.0, so anyone can build compatible tools.

# Jamboard is gone. Here’s a free replacement for teachers.

> Google shut Jamboard down on 31 December 2024. Rupok is a free, open-source whiteboard for teachers: write on slides, add AI-made activities, and bring your old Jams back as PDFs.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/jamboard/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

Google stopped Jamboard editing on 1 October 2024 and wound the app down on 31 December 2024. Your old Jams became PDFs in Google Drive. Rupok is free and open source: drop those PDFs in and keep teaching on them.

## Rupok vs Jamboard at a glance

*Rupok and Jamboard compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | Jamboard |
|---|---|---|
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | ✗ Nowhere: no editing since 1 Oct 2024, and the app wound down on 31 Dec 2024[^1] |
| Smartboards and panels | ✓ Any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari | ✗ The 55-inch Jamboard device reached end of life on 1 Oct 2024[^2] |
| File format | Open `.rpk` (a ZIP package with a published spec) | Old Jams were converted to PDFs in Google Drive[^3] |
| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Discontinued. Google pointed users to FigJam, Lucidspark and Miro[^1] |

*Jamboard no longer exists, so most rows don’t apply. The rows above are what changed.*

## Where Jamboard is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **It was simple and built into Google Workspace,** with real-time collaboration in Drive and Meet. Google’s recommended replacements (FigJam, Lucidspark and Miro)[^1] are collaborative whiteboards too. If a whole class co-editing one board is what you need today, try those: Rupok’s live class is still coming.

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **Free, with no account.** Nothing to sign up for, for you or your students.
- **Bring your Jams back.** Google converted Jams to PDFs in Drive[^3]. Download one and drop it into Rupok: every page becomes a slide you can write on.
- **Fast pen ink** on any smartboard, panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari (or the desktop app), including the classroom panel that replaced your Jamboard.
- **AI Smart Objects:** live simulations and quizzes on the slide.
- **Class replay:** students replay your lesson from a small `.rpk` file.
- **Open source,** so it can’t be switched off the way Jamboard was.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick FigJam, Lucidspark or Miro** if you mainly used Jamboard for students posting sticky notes together.

**Pick Rupok** if you used Jamboard to teach: writing on slides at the front of the class, then sharing the result.

## Bringing your Jams to Rupok

1. **Find your old Jams in Google Drive.** Google converted them to PDF files[^3]. Download the ones you want.
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and Jamboard: questions

### When did Jamboard shut down?

Google announced the wind-down on 28 September 2023. Creating and editing Jams stopped on 1 October 2024, and the app wound down on 31 December 2024[^1].

### What happened to my Jams?

Google’s help centre says Jams were converted to PDFs and are available in Google Drive[^3]. You can drop those PDFs into Rupok and write on them.

### What did Google recommend instead of Jamboard?

FigJam, Lucidspark and Miro, which integrate with Google Workspace[^1].

### What can I do with my old Jamboard device?

Google says that since 1 October 2024 the device runs unlicensed: it still works as an offline whiteboard (without saving to Drive) or as an HDMI display[^2].

## Sources

Facts about other products were checked on 23 November 2026. Prices and features change; if you spot something out of date, please [open an issue](https://github.com/Shaitrish/rupok/issues).

[^2]: [Jamboard device end of life](https://support.google.com/jamboard/answer/14084927?hl=en), Google Jamboard Help (checked 23 Nov 2026).
[^3]: [What happens to your Jams](https://support.google.com/jamboard/answer/13864841), Google Jamboard Help (checked 23 Nov 2026).

# A Microsoft Whiteboard alternative that needs no account

> Microsoft retired the standalone Whiteboard apps in October 2026 and personal accounts can no longer edit boards. Rupok is a free, no-account whiteboard for teachers. Compare, with sources.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/microsoft-whiteboard/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

In 2026 Microsoft retired the standalone Whiteboard apps, and personal Microsoft accounts lost the ability to create or edit boards. Whiteboard lives on for work and school accounts, on the web and in Teams. If that leaves you out, here’s how Rupok compares.

## Rupok vs Microsoft Whiteboard at a glance

*Rupok and Microsoft Whiteboard compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | Microsoft Whiteboard |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ◐ Included with Microsoft 365 work or school accounts. Personal accounts can’t create or edit boards since 25 Sep 2026[^2] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✗ No |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | Web and Microsoft Teams. The standalone Windows, iOS and Android apps retired on 16 Oct 2026[^1][^6] |
| Account | ✓ None, for teachers or students | Microsoft 365 work or school account[^1][^2] |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ◐ Copilot (suggest, categorize, summarize) with a paid Microsoft Copilot licence[^3] |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ✗ No lesson replay found |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | ◐ Templates, Forms polls, links and video[^5] |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ◐ Exports images; no PDF export documented[^4] |
| Smartboards and panels | ✓ Any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari | ✓ Any device with a supported browser |
| Real-time collaboration | ◷ Live class and share links: coming soon with Rupok Cloud | ✓ Real-time co-editing with cursors, and live in Teams meetings[^5] |
| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Standalone apps retired 16 Oct 2026; continues on the web and in Teams for work/school accounts[^1] |

## Where Microsoft Whiteboard is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **Real-time collaboration:** many people drawing on one board at once, with cursors, live in Teams meetings[^5]. Rupok’s live class is still coming.
- **Teams and OneDrive integration**, with school identity, compliance and storage managed by IT.
- **Copilot** to suggest, sort and summarize ideas, if your school pays for Copilot[^3].

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **No account at all.** Teachers and students just open it; personal Microsoft accounts can no longer edit Whiteboard boards[^2].
- **Made for presenting lessons:** write on PDF slides, Teach mode for the board, clicker support.
- **AI Smart Objects:** live simulations and quizzes on your slide.
- **Class replay** students open from a `.rpk` file.
- **PDF in and out:** import a PDF to teach from, and export your lesson as PDF slides or note-taking handouts.
- **Open source, with Bangla text in lessons.**

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick Microsoft Whiteboard** if your school is on Microsoft 365 and you need live co-editing in Teams meetings.

**Pick Rupok** if you teach from slides on a smartboard, don’t have a work or school Microsoft account, or want AI-made interactive lessons and replays.

## Moving your boards to Rupok

1. **Export your board.** Whiteboard exports boards as images[^4]; drop the images into Rupok, or print the board to PDF.
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and Microsoft Whiteboard: questions

### Is Microsoft Whiteboard being discontinued?

The standalone apps for Windows, iOS and Android retired on 16 October 2026. For work and school accounts, Whiteboard continues on the web and in Teams[^1].

### Can I still use Microsoft Whiteboard with a personal account?

Since 25 September 2026, personal Microsoft accounts can no longer create or edit whiteboards[^2].

### Is Rupok a good free replacement?

For teaching from slides on a board or in an online class, yes: it’s free, needs no account, and adds AI Smart Objects and replay. For live co-editing with a group, it isn’t there yet; that’s coming with Rupok Cloud.

# A free ActivInspire alternative for any panel

> A free, open-source alternative to Promethean ActivInspire for any interactive panel. Compare editions, price, platforms, AI and recording. Facts checked November 2026.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/activinspire/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

ActivInspire is Promethean’s long-running flipchart software, with a free Personal Edition and a paid Professional Edition. Rupok is free with every feature, runs in the browser, and adds AI-made lessons and class replay.

## Rupok vs ActivInspire at a glance

*Rupok and ActivInspire compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | ActivInspire |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ◐ Personal Edition is a free download; Professional comes with some ActivPanels or costs US$1,249 per device (US list price, Jan 2026)[^1][^2] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✗ No |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | Windows, macOS and Ubuntu[^1]. No web, ChromeOS or mobile app |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ✗ None found[^1] |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ◐ Screen and sound recorder in Professional only[^1] |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | ✓ Activities, polls and learner-response devices; question manager and actions in Professional[^1] |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ◐ PDF import and export in Professional only[^1] |
| Bangla | ◐ Bangla text and fonts in lessons; Bangla voice typing and settings search. Bangla interface: coming soon | ✗ About 33 interface languages, no Bangla[^1] |
| Smartboards and panels | ✓ Any smartboard, interactive panel, projector or laptop with Chrome, Edge or Safari | ✓ Works with a wide range of interactive whiteboards and panels[^1] |
| File format | Open `.rpk` (a ZIP package with a published spec) | `.flipchart`; imports SMART Notebook files[^1]; exports `.iwb`[^6] |
| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Still offered. Latest build we could verify: 3.5.18 (Jan 2025)[^3]. Promethean’s newest software is ActivSuite (launched Jan 2025)[^4] |

## Where ActivInspire is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **Years of flipcharts.** Many schools have large libraries of `.flipchart` lessons and Promethean resource packs.
- **Deep authoring tools** in Professional: actions, the question manager and self-paced learning[^1].
- **Learner-response hardware** (ActivVote, ActivExpression) and Express Poll[^1].
- **Imports SMART Notebook files**[^1] and exports IWB files[^6].

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **Every feature is free.** Replay, PDF import and PDF export (including handouts) aren’t locked behind a paid edition.
- **Runs in the browser**, on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS, with nothing to install, or as a desktop app for Windows, Mac and Linux.
- **AI Smart Objects:** live simulations and quizzes from the AI you already use.
- **Replay for every student:** a small `.rpk` file they open in any browser.
- **Bangla text in lessons** and an open file format, so lessons aren’t locked to one vendor.
- **Actively developed** in the open, with a public roadmap.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick ActivInspire** if your school has a big flipchart library, uses Promethean learner-response devices, or needs Professional’s authoring tools.

**Pick Rupok** if you want every feature free on any panel, AI-made interactive lessons, and replays students can open at home.

## Switching from ActivInspire

1. **Export from ActivInspire.** Professional exports flipcharts to PDF[^1]; with Personal Edition, print to PDF.
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and ActivInspire: questions

### Is ActivInspire being discontinued?

We found no announced end date as of November 2026. Promethean’s newest classroom software is ActivSuite[^4]. It retired ClassFlow at the end of 2023, saying that wouldn’t affect ActivInspire[^5].

### Is ActivInspire free?

The Personal Edition is a free download. The Professional Edition comes with some ActivPanels or costs US$1,249 per device on Promethean’s January 2026 US price list[^1][^2].

### Can Rupok open .flipchart files?

No. Export or print the flipchart to PDF and drop it into Rupok. (SMART Notebook can import flipcharts, if you need the objects kept.)

### Does Rupok work on a Promethean ActivPanel?

Yes, from Chrome, Edge or Safari on the panel’s computer. Rupok works with any panel’s touch and pen like any browser app.

# An Explain Everything alternative with free, unlimited replay

> Compare Rupok with Explain Everything: free plan limits, pricing, platforms, recording vs stroke replay, AI and languages. Facts checked November 2026, with sources.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/explain-everything/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

Explain Everything, now part of Promethean, records polished video lessons on tablets, with a limited free plan. Rupok replays every stroke of your class from a small file, free and without limits, and runs on your classroom board.

## Rupok vs Explain Everything at a glance

*Rupok and Explain Everything compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | Explain Everything |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ◐ Free plan: 3 projects, 1 slide per project, 3-minute videos. Advanced US$69/year (education); Pro US$7.49/month billed yearly[^1] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✗ No |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | iPad, iPhone, Android, Chromebook and a browser app[^1] |
| Account | ✓ None, for teachers or students | An account to create projects[^1] |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ◐ AI activities and an AI Companion on paid plans, on Apple devices with Apple Intelligence[^2][^5] |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ✓ Records narrated video lessons, with editing and captions; exports MP4[^2] |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | ◐ AI-made crossword, memory and matching activities; polls, timers and spinners in Advanced[^1][^5] |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ✓ Imports PDF; exports PDF, video, images and `.explain` files[^2] |

| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Actively developed; owned by Promethean since November 2022[^3] |

## Where Explain Everything is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **Polished video lessons:** record with your voice, edit, add captions and export MP4[^2]. Rupok replays strokes; replay with audio is coming.
- **Native tablet apps** for iPad, iPhone and Android that work offline[^1][^4].
- **Real-time collaboration** on paid plans[^1].
- **Many export formats:** video, PDF, images and GIFs[^2].
- **On-device AI** for activities and lesson plans on recent Apple devices[^2][^5].

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **No limits on the free plan:** unlimited lessons, pages and replay length.
- **Replay, not video:** students get every stroke in a small file. They can pause, zoom and still use the live Smart Objects, which a video can’t do.
- **AI from your own assistant**, not tied to an Apple device or a paid Explain Everything plan: chat with Claude, Codex or OpenCode inside Rupok, or paste a Smart Object from ChatGPT.
- **Built for the classroom board:** fast GPU ink on smartboards and panels in Chrome, Edge or Safari.
- **Bangla text in lessons**, and open source.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick Explain Everything** if you make narrated video lessons on an iPad, or need collaboration on tablets.

**Pick Rupok** if you teach live on a board or in an online class and want free, unlimited replays and AI-made interactive lessons.

## Switching from Explain Everything

1. **Export your project as PDF.** Explain Everything exports PDF[^2].
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and Explain Everything: questions

### Is Explain Everything free?

There’s a free plan with 3 projects, 1 slide per project and 3-minute videos. Paid plans start at US$69 a year for education (Advanced) or US$7.49 a month billed yearly (Pro)[^1].

### Who owns Explain Everything?

Promethean acquired Explain Everything in November 2022[^3].

### How is Rupok’s replay different from a video?

Rupok saves each pen stroke with its timing, so a replay redraws the lesson. The file stays small, students can zoom in, and live Smart Objects keep working. It has no sound yet; replay with audio is coming.

# Rupok vs OneNote for teaching on a board

> OneNote is a great notebook; Rupok is built for teaching from a smartboard. Compare price, ink replay, AI, Class Notebook, platforms and Bangla. Facts checked November 2026.

Canonical: https://rupok.app/compare/onenote/ · Language: en · Updated: 2026-11-23

Many teachers write on OneNote at the front of the class. OneNote is a superb notebook for every device. Rupok is built for presenting: slides, a Teach mode for the board, live AI-made objects, and a replay students can open anywhere.

## Rupok vs OneNote at a glance

*Rupok and OneNote compared, as of November 2026*

|  | Rupok | OneNote |
|---|---|---|
| Price | ✓ Free, every feature, on every device. No licence keys | ◐ Free to download and use; Ink Replay, Math Assistant and Copilot need Microsoft 365 or Copilot subscriptions[^1][^5] |
| Open source | ✓ Yes: AGPL-3.0. The `.rpk` format spec is Apache-2.0 | ✗ No |
| Runs on | Chrome, Edge or Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux and ChromeOS. Desktop app for Windows, macOS (beta) and Linux; installers not code-signed yet | Windows, Mac, web, iPhone, iPad and Android[^1] |
| Account | ✓ None, for teachers or students | A Microsoft account (the Windows app can also keep local notebooks)[^1] |
| AI | ✓ Your own AI (Claude, Codex or OpenCode): chat with it inside Rupok, let it edit the open board live, or connect it over MCP. It makes live Smart Objects and writes step-by-step solutions in handwriting (Solve this). HTML from any chatbot works too | ◐ Copilot summarizes, rewrites and answers questions, with a paid subscription[^5] |
| Replay and recording | ✓ Stroke-by-stroke replay of every page, built in. Replay with audio: coming soon | ◐ Ink Replay redraws strokes in order, on Windows only[^2] |
| Interactive content | ✓ AI-made simulations, 3D models and quizzes that run live on the slide, plus a gallery of ready-made presets (physics, chemistry, maths, ICT, history, quiz) | Notes, ink and embedded files |
| PDF and slides | ✓ Import a PDF and write on every page; export slides, or handouts with 2 or 3 slides per page and lines for notes | ✓ Insert PDF printouts and ink on them; export to PDF[^8] |
| Bangla | ◐ Bangla text and fonts in lessons; Bangla voice typing and settings search. Bangla interface: coming soon | ◐ Bangla (Bangladesh) gets proofing tools only; Bangla (India) is partly localized[^6] |
| Offline | ✓ The desktop app works without internet, including maths recognition (AI features need internet). In the browser, the board runs on your device once it is open | ✓ Native apps work offline and sync later[^9] |
| Real-time collaboration | ◷ Live class and share links: coming soon with Rupok Cloud | ✓ Co-editing; Class Notebook gives each student a private section[^3] |
| Status (Nov 2026) | Actively developed: early alpha, v0.2.0 released 23 Nov 2026 | Actively developed. OneNote for Windows 10 reached end of support on 14 Oct 2025[^4] |

## Where OneNote is stronger

Being honest about this saves you time.

- **Notebooks on every device**, with offline work and sync[^1][^9].
- **Class Notebook:** private student sections, a read-only content library, a collaboration space, page distribution and feedback, with rosters from Teams or an LMS[^3].
- **Co-editing** and a huge Microsoft 365 ecosystem; Office 365 A1 is free for eligible schools[^7].
- **Math Assistant and handwriting search** (Math Assistant needs a qualifying subscription). Rupok reads handwritten maths offline, and Solve this writes worked solutions with your own AI.

## Where Rupok is stronger

- **Built for presenting:** slide pages, a Teach mode that keeps the slide fitted to the board, and clicker support.
- **Live Smart Objects:** simulations and quizzes made by your AI, running on the slide.
- **Replay anywhere:** students replay every stroke in any browser. OneNote’s Ink Replay is Windows-only[^2].
- **No account** for teachers or students.
- **Fast GPU ink** that stays smooth through a long class.
- **Open source,** with Bangla text in lessons.

## Which one should you pick?

**Pick OneNote** for class notebooks, homework distribution and notes across every device in a Microsoft 365 school.

**Pick Rupok** for teaching at the board: writing on slides, live AI-made objects, and replays for students.

Plenty of teachers use both: OneNote for the notebook, Rupok for the lesson.

## Moving a OneNote lesson to Rupok

1. **Export the pages as PDF.** OneNote exports pages, sections or notebooks to PDF on Windows, and single pages on the web and Mac[^8].
2. **Open the board.** Go to [rupok.app/board](https://rupok.app/board/) in Chrome, Edge or Safari, on the panel's PC or your laptop. No install, no account. Prefer an app? [Download it](https://rupok.app/download/) for Windows, Mac or Linux.
3. **Drop the PDF in.** Every page becomes a slide you can write on.
4. **Add the live parts.** Ask your AI for a simulation or quiz and drop it on a slide as a Smart Object ([how](https://rupok.app/ai-whiteboard/)).
5. **Save and share.** Save the lesson as a `.rpk` file and send it to students. They replay it at [rupok.app/open](https://rupok.app/open/).

## Rupok and OneNote: questions

### Is OneNote free for teachers?

OneNote is free to download and use. Some features, such as Ink Replay and Math Assistant, and Copilot need a Microsoft 365 or Copilot subscription[^1][^5]. Eligible schools can get Office 365 A1 for free[^7].

### Does OneNote replay handwriting?

Yes, Ink Replay redraws strokes in order, but only on Windows[^2]. Rupok’s replay works in any browser, including students’ phones.

### Should I switch from OneNote to Rupok?

Not necessarily. Keep OneNote for notebooks and use Rupok for presenting at the board, where slides, live objects and replay matter.
